subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should OpenClaw preserve `reason: "target-none"` as the machine-readable heartbeat skip reason and add an additive human-facing disabled-delivery hint, or rename the reason itself?
rationale: The code change is small, but the exposed reason string may be consumed by scripts/log parsers and the alternative adds a new optional diagnostic field.

options.title: Add an additive hint
options.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a human-readable disabled-delivery hint, and render that hint in heartbeat status output.

options.title: Rename the reason
options.body: Change the machine reason to `delivery-disabled` and accept the possible compatibility break for private consumers.

options.title: Leave current output
options.body: Keep the raw diagnostic unchanged and accept the ongoing operator confusion as low priority.

recommendation.title: Add an additive hint
recommendation.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a human-readable disabled-delivery hint, and render that hint in heartbeat status output.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the default-`none` heartbeat change and were directly asked on the closed additive repair PR.
